title: Movement and speed
about: Collocations for speed and movement: different words for fast (a quick glance, rapid growth, a speedy recovery, a brisk walk, a hasty decision), slow movement and stopping (in slow motion, come to a standstill), and changes of speed and direction (pick up speed, take a shortcut, lose your balance).

parts.title: Changes in speed, movement and direction
Which word for fast?
parts.note: Усі ці прикметники перекладаються як «швидкий», але кожен має своїх партнерів. Зірочкою позначено офіційніші слова: rapid, speedy, swift, prompt — їх частіше почуєш у новинах, листах і на роботі. У звичайній розмові найчастіше кажуть fast (про те, що швидко рухається чи працює) і quick (про те, що триває недовго). Hasty завжди з відтінком «занадто поспішно».

rows: everyday: moves or works at speed
look, glance, answer, decision, shower, lunch
growth, decline, change, progress, increase, movement
more formal: often about people in charge
more formal: on time, without delay

items.pattern: a fast car / train / computer · the fast train (to …) · at a fast pace
items.meaning: a car, train or machine that can move or work at high speed; the fast train is the one that makes fewer stops
items.example: My grandad still drives a **fast car**, even at seventy-five.
more: The **fast train** doesn't stop at our village, so we take the slow one.
We walked at a **fast pace** to keep warm.
items.watchOut: Про машини, поїзди й техніку, які швидко їдуть чи працюють, кажуть fast: a fast car, the fast train. Не rapid train і не speedy train. Британці про машину іноді кажуть і a quick car, але fast — найзвичайніше.

items.pattern: drive / be in the fast lane · (figurative) life in the fast lane
items.meaning: the motorway lane for overtaking, where cars go fastest; figuratively, an exciting, busy way of life
items.example: Dad always drives in the **fast lane**, and Mum always tells him to slow down.
more: A police car flew past us in the **fast lane**.
After twenty years of **life in the fast lane**, he moved to a quiet farm.
items.watchOut: Смуга на дорозі — lane, а не line (line — лінія розмітки). У Британії рух лівосторонній, тож the fast lane — крайня права смуга. Life in the fast lane — бурхливе, шалене життя.

items.pattern: have / take a quick look (at sth) · give sb / sth a quick glance
items.meaning: a short look at something, just for a moment
items.example: Can you have a **quick look** at the washing machine? It's making a strange noise.
more: She gave me a **quick glance** and smiled.
I had a **quick look** in the fridge, but there was nothing for dinner.
items.watchOut: «Глянути» — have / take a quick look, а не make a look. З look і glance не кажуть fast чи speedy: a quick glance, а не a fast glance.

items.pattern: have a quick shower / lunch / coffee · grab a quick lunch
items.meaning: a short one that doesn't take long, usually because you're busy
items.example: I'll just have a **quick shower** and then we can go out.
more: We stopped at a café for a **quick lunch** on our way to the coast.
Have you got time for a **quick coffee** before your train?
items.watchOut: «Прийняти душ» — have (або take) a shower, а не accept a shower. Про короткі щоденні справи кажуть quick, а не rapid: a quick lunch, а не a rapid lunch.

items.pattern: a quick answer / reply / decision · make a quick decision · give sb a quick answer
items.meaning: given or made in a short time; neutral, not a criticism
items.example: The shop needs a **quick answer**: do we want the sofa in blue or grey?
more: It was a **quick decision**: we saw the flat and signed the contract the same day.
Thanks for the **quick reply**. See you on Saturday!
items.watchOut: Quick decision — просто швидке рішення, часто це навіть добре. Hasty decision — поспішне, необдумане, про яке потім шкодують.

items.pattern: a rapid increase / decline / change (in sth) · rapid growth / movement
items.meaning: a big change that happens in a short time, often in numbers or prices
items.example: There's been a **rapid increase** in the price of butter this year.
more: Doctors were surprised by the **rapid change** in his condition.
We've noticed a **rapid decline** in the number of hedgehogs in our garden.
items.watchOut: Про цифри, ціни й тенденції зазвичай кажуть rapid: a rapid increase in prices. Quick increase так зазвичай не кажуть. «Стрімке зростання» — rapid growth, зазвичай без a.

items.pattern: make rapid progress (with / in sth)
items.meaning: improve or move forward quickly
items.example: My dad started learning the guitar at sixty and made **rapid progress**.
more: Work on the new swimming pool is making **rapid progress**: it should open in May.
Children often make **rapid progress** when they live abroad for a year.
items.watchOut: «Досягати успіхів, прогресувати» — make progress, а не do progress. Progress незлічуване: не a progress і не progresses.

items.pattern: make a speedy recovery · wish sb a speedy recovery · also a quick / swift recovery
items.meaning: getting well again quickly after an illness, injury or operation
items.example: We sent Grandma flowers and a card wishing her a **speedy recovery**.
more: The vet says our cat should make a **speedy recovery** after the operation.
Young people usually make a **speedy recovery** from this kind of injury.
items.watchOut: «Швидко одужати» — make a speedy recovery, а не do a recovery. «Швидкого одужання!» — Wishing you a speedy recovery! або Get well soon! Brisk і prompt з recovery не вживають.

items.pattern: bring sth / come to a speedy conclusion · also speedy access (to sth), a speedy response
items.meaning: a quick end to something, such as a meeting, an argument or a process; a bit formal
items.example: Both families wanted a **speedy conclusion** to the argument about the fence.
more: The new bridge gives **speedy access** to the city centre.
We were pleased with the council's **speedy response** to our complaint.
items.watchOut: Speedy звучить трохи офіційно. У розмові частіше кажуть finish quickly або a quick end. «Швидкий доступ до…» — speedy access to sth, з прийменником to.

items.pattern: take swift action (to do sth) · a swift response / reaction (to sth)
items.meaning: action or a reaction that comes very quickly; a bit formal, often about people in charge
items.example: The head teacher took **swift action** when she heard about the bullying.
more: Thanks to the **swift response** of the fire brigade, nobody was hurt.
My complaint got a **swift reaction**: the manager phoned me within an hour.
items.watchOut: «Вжити заходів, діяти» — take action, а не make action чи do action. Action тут зазвичай незлічуване: take swift action, без a.

items.pattern: prompt payment (of sth) · a prompt reply / response · pay / reply promptly · be prompt with payment
items.meaning: done immediately or on time, without any delay
items.example: Some companies give a small discount for **prompt payment**.
more: I wrote to the council and got a **prompt reply** the next morning.
Thanks for your **prompt reply**. I'll book the tickets today.
items.watchOut: Prompt — без затримки, вчасно; так часто пишуть в офіційних листах і рахунках. Не плутай з дієсловом prompt — спонукати, підштовхнути (What prompted you to call?).

items.pattern: go for / have / take a brisk walk · at a brisk pace · with brisk efficiency
items.meaning: a walk at a quick, energetic speed, often for exercise; brisk = quick and full of energy
items.example: A **brisk walk** in the fresh air always wakes me up.
more: We set off at a **brisk pace** to get to the top before dark.
The receptionist checked us in with **brisk efficiency**.
items.watchOut: A quick walk — радше коротка прогулянка; a brisk walk — енергійна, швидким кроком, часто для здоров'я. Про машини й поїзди brisk не кажуть: не a brisk car.

items.pattern: business / trade is brisk · do brisk business
items.meaning: a lot of buying and selling; many customers
items.example: Umbrella sellers were doing **brisk business** outside the station when it started to rain.
more: Business was **brisk** at the bakery on the morning before Easter.
The second-hand bookshop does **brisk business** in summer, when the tourists arrive.
items.watchOut: «Торгівля йде жваво» — business / trade is brisk. Не business is fast і не quick business. Простіше — The shop was really busy.

items.pattern: make a hasty decision · come to / draw a hasty conclusion · hasty words
items.meaning: made or said too quickly, without enough thought, so it may be wrong
items.example: Selling the house after one bad winter was a **hasty decision**.
more: Looking back, I think we came to a **hasty conclusion** about the new neighbours.
My uncle made a **hasty decision** to buy a boat and sold it a month later.
items.watchOut: Hasty — завжди з відтінком «занадто поспішно, без роздумів». Quick decision — просто швидке рішення. «Робити поспішні висновки» — draw hasty conclusions або jump to conclusions.

items.pattern: make a hasty exit (from sth) · also a quick / swift exit
items.meaning: leave a place very quickly, often because you are embarrassed or want to avoid someone
items.example: When his ex walked into the café, Max made a **hasty exit** through the back door.
more: The fox made a **hasty exit** when our dog started barking.
I'd forgotten my old classmate's name, so I made a **hasty exit** before she noticed.
items.watchOut: Кажуть make a hasty exit, а не do an exit. Вихід як дія — exit; output — це «продукція, результат», а outlet — торгова точка або розетка.

items.pattern: a top speed of … · reach a top speed of … · at top speed
items.meaning: the highest speed that something can go
items.uk: максимальна швидкість; щодуху, на повній швидкості
items.example: Cheetahs can reach a **top speed** of over 100 kilometres an hour.
more: The kids ran out of school at **top speed** when the bell rang.
Our little boat has a **top speed** of only ten knots.
items.watchOut: «Максимальна швидкість» — top speed (або maximum speed). Peak speed і highest speed тут зазвичай не кажуть. At top speed — «щодуху, на повній швидкості».

items.pattern: at breakneck speed / pace · drive / ride / run at breakneck speed
items.meaning: dangerously fast, without enough care
items.example: The delivery driver raced down our street at **breakneck speed**.
more: The ambulance drove through the town at **breakneck speed**.
Life in the city moves at a **breakneck pace**.
items.watchOut: Breakneck — одне слово, буквально «скрутити в'язи». Не neckbreak. Зазвичай без артикля: at breakneck speed (але at a breakneck pace).

items.pattern: show / watch / film sth in slow motion · a slow-motion replay
items.meaning: shown more slowly than in real life, so you can see every movement
items.example: On TV they showed the horse jumping the fence in **slow motion**.
more: My phone can film in **slow motion**, so I recorded the kids jumping into the pool.
Everything seemed to happen in **slow motion** as the glass fell off the table.
items.watchOut: «Уповільнена зйомка» — slow motion, а не slow movement і не slow mode. Прийменник in: in slow motion. Перед іменником — через дефіс: a slow-motion replay.

items.pattern: slow-moving traffic / queue · be stuck in slow-moving traffic
items.meaning: traffic that is moving, but very slowly
items.example: We were stuck in **slow-moving traffic** all the way to the coast.
more: Expect **slow-moving traffic** near the stadium on match days.
There was a long, **slow-moving** queue outside the museum.
items.watchOut: Найуживаніше — slow-moving traffic, з дефісом. Traffic незлічуване: не a traffic і не traffics. Затор — a traffic jam.

items.pattern: the traffic slows to a crawl · slowed to a crawl
items.meaning: become so slow that it is hardly moving
items.example: As we got closer to the city centre, the traffic **slowed to a crawl**.
more: The queue for the toilets **slowed to a crawl** during the break.
In the thick fog, cars on the motorway **slowed to a crawl**.
items.watchOut: Crawl — повзти, як немовля. Slow to a crawl — ще рухаються, але дуже повільно; come to a standstill — повністю зупинилися.

items.pattern: come to / grind to a standstill · bring sth to a standstill
items.meaning: stop moving completely
items.example: The train **came to a standstill** in the middle of a field, and nobody told us why.
more: Work on our new kitchen **came to a standstill** when the builder got ill.
The queue **came to a standstill** when the till broke.
items.watchOut: «Рух став» — the traffic came to a standstill, а не the traffic stood. Артикль a обов'язковий. Схоже: come to a halt / come to a stop.

items.pattern: do sth in an unhurried manner / way · at an unhurried pace
items.meaning: slowly and calmly, without rushing; it can suggest that someone is a bit too slow
items.example: The old man counted his change in an **unhurried manner** while the queue grew behind him.
more: Our new doctor talks in a calm, **unhurried manner**, which makes you feel safe.
We walked round the market at an **unhurried pace**.
items.watchOut: Unhurried, а не unhurrying. Слово трохи книжне й часто з легким докором: людина надто повільна. Без докору, коли повільно й приємно, — leisurely.

items.pattern: a leisurely breakfast / lunch / stroll · at a leisurely pace
items.meaning: done in a relaxed way, without hurrying, because you are enjoying it
items.example: On holiday we have a **leisurely breakfast** on the terrace every morning.
more: After lunch we went for a **leisurely stroll** round the village.
We spent a **leisurely** afternoon reading in the garden.
items.watchOut: Вимова: /ˈleʒəli/ (британською). Не плутай із leisure (іменник): leisure time — вільний час, але a leisurely breakfast. Leisurely — повільно й із задоволенням, без докору.

items.pattern: be painfully slow · painfully slow progress / service · painfully slowly
items.meaning: so slow that it is annoying or upsetting
items.example: Our old lift is **painfully slow**, so I usually take the stairs.
more: Learning to drive was a **painfully slow** process for me.
My son reads **painfully slowly**, but he's getting better.
items.watchOut: Painfully тут не про біль, а «нестерпно, аж дратує». Перед прикметником потрібен прислівник: painfully slow, а не painful slow. Так само painfully shy — болісно сором'язливий.

items.pattern: gather / pick up speed · gathered / picked up speed
items.meaning: start to move faster
items.example: The bus **gathered speed** once it left the town.
more: The boat **picked up speed** as we left the harbour.
Our plans for the wedding are finally **gathering speed**.
items.watchOut: «Набирати швидкість» — gather / pick up speed (ще gain speed), без артикля. Не collect speed і не take speed.

items.pattern: take a shortcut (through / across sth) · also a short cut
items.meaning: go a shorter way than the usual one
items.example: We **took a shortcut** through the churchyard and got to school on time.
more: Never **take a shortcut** along the railway line.
Is there a **shortcut** to the beach from here?
items.watchOut: «Зрізати шлях» — take a shortcut, а не cut the way. Британці часто пишуть окремо: a short cut.

items.pattern: make / take a detour (through / round sth) · a short / long detour
items.meaning: go a different, longer way, e.g. because a road is closed or to visit something on the way
items.example: Because of the marathon, all the buses are **taking a detour** round the park.
more: It's worth **making a detour** to see the waterfall.
The satnav sent us on a long **detour** through tiny villages.
items.watchOut: Detour /ˈdiːtʊə/ — об'їзд, довша дорога. Не плутай із bypass — об'їзна дорога навколо міста. Знак об'їзду на британських дорогах — Diversion.

items.pattern: lose your balance · keep your balance
items.meaning: become unsteady, so that you fall or almost fall
items.example: Grandma **lost her balance** on the stairs, so we've put in a second handrail.
more: The waiter **lost his balance** and dropped a tray of glasses.
Hold my hand so you don't **lose your balance**.
items.watchOut: «Втратити рівновагу» — lose your balance, з присвійним займенником: I lost my balance. Не missed і не dropped. Протилежне — keep your balance.

items.pattern: lose / miss your footing (on sth)
items.meaning: your feet slip, so you are no longer standing firmly and may fall
items.example: The path was covered in wet leaves, and I **lost my footing** more than once.
more: Hold the rope so you don't **lose your footing** on the rocks.
The horse **lost its footing** in the mud and fell.
items.watchOut: Lose your footing — ноги зісковзнули (мокрі камені, багнюка, схил). Lose your balance — ширше: тіло втратило рівновагу. Не lose your foot і не lose your legs.

items.pattern: steer the conversation (away from sth / towards sth / round to sth)
items.meaning: gently change what people are talking about
items.example: When Grandpa started complaining about his neighbours, Mum **steered the conversation** towards the garden.
more: A good host knows how to **steer the conversation** away from arguments.
She always **steers the conversation** round to her new car.
items.watchOut: Steer — кермувати, тут образно. Не drive the conversation. Ще можна turn the conversation to sth або просто change the subject.

items.pattern: take a step / a few steps (towards / back / forward) · take your first steps
items.meaning: walk a very short distance
items.example: After the operation, Dad **took a few steps** round the ward with a nurse.
more: Every time I **took a step**, the old floorboards creaked.
He **took a few steps** into the dark garden and called the cat.
items.watchOut: «Зробити крок» — take a step, а не make a step. Перші кроки дитини — take your first steps.

items.pattern: turn sth upside down · be upside down · (figurative) turn a place upside down (looking for sth)
items.meaning: turn something so that the top is at the bottom; also, make a place very untidy while looking for something
items.uk: перевернути догори дриґом; перевернути все догори дном
items.example: I **turned** the box **upside down**, and all the old photos fell out.
more: Burglars had **turned** the bedroom **upside down**, but they didn't find the money.
That picture's **upside down**. Turn it the right way up!
items.watchOut: «Догори ногами, догори дриґом» — upside down, а не with legs up. Не плутай з inside out — навиворіт (про одяг). Дієслово — turn: turn sth upside down, а не take.

items.pattern: go astray (letters, parcels, luggage) · went / gone astray
items.meaning: get lost and not arrive where it was sent
items.example: My birthday card to Gran **went astray**, so I sent another one.
more: Half of our post **went astray** when we moved house.
If a parcel **goes astray**, the shop will send you a new one.
items.watchOut: Go astray, а не get astray. Схоже — go missing, get lost. Обережно: lead sb astray — збити когось на манівці (про погану компанію).

warmup.q: He took a ___ glance at his watch.
warmup.explain: Швидкий погляд — a quick glance (або look). Fast і speedy з glance не вживають.
Поспішне, необдумане рішення — a hasty decision (ще a rushed decision). Rushing тут не підходить, а brisk — про ходу й торгівлю.

warmup.q: This moped has a ___ speed of 45 km/h.
warmup.explain: Максимальна швидкість — top speed (або maximum speed). High speed — просто «висока швидкість», так максимум не називають.

warmup.uk: Покажіть цей момент ще раз в уповільненому режимі!
warmup.q: Show that moment again in slow ___!
warmup.explain: Уповільнена зйомка — slow motion: in slow motion. Slow movement і slow mode так не кажуть.

warmup.uk: Через аварію рух на трасі повністю зупинився.
warmup.q: Because of an accident, the traffic on the motorway came to a ___.
warmup.explain: Повністю зупинитися (про рух) — come to a standstill (або come to a halt / stop).
Набирати швидкість — pick up speed або gather speed. Collect speed і take speed так не кажуть.

warmup.q: Let's ___ a shortcut through the market.
warmup.explain: Зрізати шлях — take a shortcut. Cut тут не підходить: «зрізати» вже є в самому слові shortcut.

warmup.uk: Частина нашого багажу загубилася в аеропорту.
warmup.q: Some of our luggage went ___ at the airport.
warmup.explain: Загубитися дорогою — go astray (або go missing). Went lost — помилка: кажуть got lost.

A.q: The nurse said the operation went well, and she expects a ___ recovery.
A.explain: Швидке одужання — a speedy (або quick) recovery. Brisk — про ходу й торгівлю, prompt — про оплату й відповіді.

A.q: The market stall sold all its strawberries by ten. Business was ___.
A.explain: Торгівля йде жваво — business is brisk. Fast і rapid з business так не кажуть.

A.q: Take your time. A ___ decision now could cost you a lot of money later.
A.explain: Hasty decision — поспішне, необдумане рішення. Brisk і breakneck з decision не вживають.

B.q: The nature film showed a hummingbird's wings in slow ___.
B.explain: Уповільнена зйомка — in slow motion. Slow movement і slow mode так не кажуть.

B.q: Two buses got stuck in the narrow street, and everything came to a ___.
B.explain: Повністю зупинитися — come to a standstill. Stillness — тиша, нерухомість, але з come to a його не вживають.

B.q: There's no rush. Let's have a ___ walk round the old town before dinner.
B.explain: Leisurely — неквапливий, із задоволенням. Leisure — іменник (вільний час), hasty — поспішний.

C.q: As the roller coaster went down the first drop, it ___ up speed.
C.explain: Набирати швидкість — pick up speed (або gather speed).

C.q: Our postcard from Spain never arrived. It must have ___ astray.
C.explain: Загубитися дорогою — go astray: must have gone astray. Get astray — помилка.

C.q: At the family dinner, I ___ the conversation away from my new boyfriend.
C.explain: Перевести розмову на іншу тему — steer the conversation (away from / towards sth). Drive тут не кажуть.

example.title: Sunday on two wheels
example.uk:
Минулої неділі ми неквапливо поснідали, а потім поїхали на велосипедах до моря. Головну дорогу перекрили, тож ми поїхали в об'їзд через ліс. Потім брат запропонував зрізати шлях через поле. Там було так багнисто, що я втратив рівновагу й упав у калюжу.

Коли ми спускалися з великого пагорба, мій велосипед набрав швидкість, і я на шаленій швидкості пролетів повз ферму. Унизу рух повністю зупинився, тож ми повели велосипеди повз машини.

На пляжі в кафе жваво торгували, і нам довелося стояти в черзі за напоями. Удома я швиденько прийняв душ і заснув на дивані.
example.en:
Last Sunday we had a [[leisurely breakfast|b6]] and then cycled to the coast. The main road was closed, so we [[made a detour|c3]] through the woods. Then my brother suggested we [[take a shortcut|c2]] across a field. It was so muddy that I [[lost my balance|c4]] and fell into a puddle.

On the way down the big hill, my bike [[picked up speed|c1]], and I flew past a farm [[at breakneck speed|a17]]. At the bottom, the traffic had [[come to a standstill|b4]], so we walked our bikes past the cars.

At the beach, the café was doing [[brisk business|a13]], and we had to queue for drinks. Back home, I had a [[quick shower|a4]] and fell asleep on the sofa.
